description: §18.5 NESTED-STATEMENT-FIDELITY axis — a keywordless bare assignment written inside a NESTED block of a value-position match arm must lower as an ASSIGNMENT to the enclosing binding, never as a fresh declaration. scrml's parser surfaces `a = 1` in a body position as a decl-shaped node, and the emitter's decl-vs-assignment decision keys on the enclosing scope's declared-name set; where that set failed to reach the nested statement, `for (…) { a = 1 }` emitted `for (…) { const a = 1 }` — a SHADOWING binding, so the loop no longer wrote the outer `a` and the lifted tail read the pre-loop value. The self-referencing spelling `a = a + 1` emitted `const a = a + 1`, a TDZ ReferenceError at RUNTIME that `node --check` accepts as valid syntax — which is why this case asserts VALUES and not emitted text.
rationale: §18.5 arm bodies compose with §13 statement semantics: an assignment inside a nested block writes the binding already in scope. Two spellings are pinned because they fail differently and only one of them is loud. The bare form `{ let a = 0; for (…) { a = 1 } a }` is SILENT when broken — it yields the pre-loop 0 instead of 1, a wrong value with no diagnostic. The self-referencing form `{ let a = 10; for (…) { a = a + 1 } a }` is FATAL when broken — a shadowing `const a = a + 1` reads `a` in its own temporal dead zone and throws. Both must hold in every value position: derived cell (1, 12), return statement (21), multi-scrutinee decl (§18.19, 30), `fn` local decl (42), and `function` local decl (50, 62). The self-referencing totals are accumulations over two iterations, so a fix that merely stopped shadowing but dropped the write would still be caught.
